data.title: KH Group Oyj's (HEL:KHG) Soft Earnings Don't Show The Whole Picture
data.description:
KH Group Oyj's (HEL:KHG) earnings announcement last week didn't impress shareholders. However, our analysis suggests that the soft headline numbers are getting counterbalanced by some positive underlying factors.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Examining Cashflow Against KH Group Oyj's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

For the year to September 2026, KH Group Oyj had an accrual ratio of -0.19. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of €23m, well over the €1.38m it reported in profit. KH Group Oyj's free cash flow improved over the last year, which is generally good to see.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On KH Group Oyj's Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, KH Group Oyj produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Based on this observation, we consider it possible that KH Group Oyj's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! On the other hand, its EPS actually shrunk in the last twelve months. data.title: Voya Financial (VOYA) Stock Could Be Undervalued Despite Its 63% Run
data.description:
Voya Financial has logged strong share price gains over the past several years, and that kind of run naturally prompts a question about what the business is actually earning on the capital it puts to work. With the stock now around recent highs, investors are increasingly asking whether those returns on capital are enough to support where the valuation sits today.

  • Over the past 5 years, Voya Financial has returned 63.3%, which puts real weight on whether the company’s capital returns can keep justifying that kind of long haul performance.
  • Activist pressure around governance and capital allocation, alongside Voya’s push to expand areas like pooled employer retirement plans and stop loss insurance, can influence how effectively fresh capital is deployed and what that might mean for future profitability on each new dollar invested.
  • If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why Voya Financial's 15.1x P/E tells a different valuation story.

The issue now is whether the returns Voya Financial earns on its capital line up with the current share price or ask investors to accept a thinner margin of safety.

To see how Voya Financial’s capital returns compare with other opportunities using similar criteria, review companies in the 39 high quality undervalued stocks

Is Voya Financial Still Cheap on Excess Returns?

The Excess Returns model looks at how much profit Voya Financial can generate above the cost of its equity capital. Here, the key input is a stable earnings figure of $8.29 per share built on an average Return on Equity of 16.12%, compared with a Book Value base of $42.48 per share that is projected to grow to a Stable Book Value of $51.41 per share. After accounting for a Cost of Equity of $4.21 per share, the analysis points to an Excess Return of $4.07 per share. This is the surplus value creation the model focuses on rather than near term cash swings.

That spread between what Voya Financial is expected to earn and what it needs to earn to justify its equity cost feeds into an estimated intrinsic value that sits substantially above the current share price of $99.01. The activist no confidence campaign from TOMS Capital helps explain why the market may still discount those projected returns, despite the model implying stronger value creation on existing and future equity.
